summary: A command-line tool and a Claude Code plugin that run on your machine and read your repos. There is no server and no user data held anywhere. npm hosts the package, and GitHub Actions publishes it.

headlines.label: Known cost a month
headlines.note: No npm, GitHub or Claude bill is recorded. The package is free and MIT.

headlines.label: Servers we run
headlines.note: Everything is local except a version lookup on npm and a one-time Quartz clone.

headlines.label: Biggest risk
headlines.note: canon check runs any commands: a repo's context.yaml declares, through sh -c. Run it only on repos you trust.

headlines.label: Release trigger
headlines.note: Pushing a new version to main publishes to npm. No other step is needed.

flows.name: Release a version
flows.note: a push to main with a new version
steps: A push to main, a v* tag or a manual run starts the job. One release runs at a time.
It installs, runs typecheck and tests, and fails if package.json and plugin.json have different versions.
It asks npm whether that version exists. If it does, it stops there.
Otherwise it runs npm publish with provenance, using the NPM_TOKEN secret.
Then it tags the commit and makes the GitHub release.

flows.name: Run canon check
flows.note: also runs in a repo's pre-push hook
steps: The CLI reads .context/context.yaml and the repo's .context.
It runs each built-in check, then each command the config declares, through sh -c in the repo.

flows.name: Update canon
steps: It fetches the latest version from the npm registry.
From a git checkout it only tells you to pull. Otherwise it runs npm or pnpm install -g.
It then updates the Claude Code plugin and asks you to restart Claude Code.

flows.name: Weigh a request
flows.note: canon weigh, or the skill inside a session
steps: canon weigh runs claude -p with your request.
Claude reads the repo's wiki and rules and answers do it, do it differently or push back.
The verdict is appended to .context/raw/canon/verdicts.jsonl in the repo.

flows.name: Start a session
flows.note: every Claude Code session in a repo with the plugin
steps: The hook starts qmd update in the background and does not wait.
It puts the constitution's principle titles in front of the session.

flows.name: Serve the wiki
steps: First run: git clone Quartz, check out the pinned commit, npm ci.
It builds every product's wiki and serves it on localhost, port 4610 by default.

data.where: Stay on your machine. check, search and ui send nothing out.
One GET to registry.npmjs.org; no repo data in it

data.what: A request given to canon weigh
data.where: Sent to Claude, as any Claude Code prompt is

unknowns: The real monthly bill: nothing records npm or Claude usage cost. GitHub Actions was $0 net for October 2026.
RISK: the commands: list in context.yaml runs through sh -c on every canon check, including the pre-push hook and --all. A repo you did not write can run code on your machine.
RISK: the release only tags and makes the GitHub release when it publishes. If npm publish works and the tag step fails, a rerun sees the version on npm, skips both, and the tag is never made.
RISK: the session hook starts a detached qmd update at every session start, with no check for one already running. The load from many sessions is not measured.
How the release signs in to npm: it passes the NPM_TOKEN secret and also asks for provenance. Whether a long-lived token is still needed is not read.
What qmd downloads or sends on its first embed is not read here; it is a separate tool.
